summary: Two residential towers at 250 and 260 King Street, for which the Department of Building Inspection filed new-construction permits in November 2000 (17 stories each; 279 and 307 dwelling units) and recorded both permits with a completed date of 2004-10-06 (a permit closeout date; the permit for 260 King Street now carries the status 'reinstated'); the Assessor roll gives 2004 as year built for the condominium lots at 250 King Street, and two listing sites give 595 residential units and Catellus as developer.

milestones.text: Department of Building Inspection new-construction permit applications 200011306843 (250 King St: 17 stories, 279 dwelling units, mixed use) and 200011306844 (260 King St: 17 stories, 307 units, mixed use) filed, each with an estimated cost of $73,000,000

Department of Building Inspection records both new-construction permits as completed on 2004-10-06 (a permit closeout date, not an occupancy date); the Assessor roll lists 2004 as year built for the condominium lots at 250 King St. The listing site SFHighrises gives "Year Built: 2003", which conflicts; the conflict is not resolved

facts.value: Permits propose 279 (250 King St) and 307 (260 King St) dwelling units, 586 together; two listing sites give 595 residential units. The counts are not reconciled.

open_questions: Developer is stated only by a listing site (SFHighrises); the Catellus Mission Bay page cited in the map's geometry file does not mention The Beacon. No primary source read confirms it.
Architect not recorded: Afi + Associates says Skidmore, Owings and Merrill; other attributions seen earlier by the project are unsourced here.

The permits do not use the name 'The Beacon'; the link from the name to 250 and 260 King St rests on the OpenStreetMap addr:housename tag cited in the geometry file and on SFHighrises and Afi + Associates, which both give 250 and 260 King St.
No construction start date or opening month found; the permit completed date is a closeout date, not an occupancy date.
The building permit for 260 King St has status 'reinstated' in the Department of Building Inspection data; the meaning is not explained in the data.

The AT&T store at 236 King St is shown as closed on the strength of a Yelp listing that showed it closed as of March 2025 (that is when the listing was seen, not when the store closed); the listing could not be opened again (HTTP 403 on 2026-10-12) and no other page about the store was found. No opening or closing date is known. The address is assigned to The Beacon by Pier & Point; the listing does not name the building.

Update 2026-10-12, completion year: readable sources conflict. The Department of Building Inspection's data records both new-construction permits as completed on 2004-10-06 and the Assessor roll gives year built 2004 for 593 of 595 lots on King St, while SFHighrises (a listing site) says "Year Built: 2003". A permit closeout can follow occupancy, so 2003 is not ruled out and 2004 is not confirmed as the opening year; the timeline shows only the 2004-10 permit closeout, not a 2003 date.
